title: Support ticket routing
when_to_use: Route the primary request to one support team; inspect impact and refund intent independently.
notes: Define ownership in code. These synthetic labels are educational, not a support benchmark.

title: Agent next-tool selection
when_to_use: Choose among a small, available set of read-only capabilities.
notes: Code enforces tool permissions, validates arguments, and executes only an allowed tool. Missing inputs should be collected before execution.

title: Continue, retry, ask, or stop
when_to_use: Interpret the latest observation in a bounded agent loop.
notes: Retry budgets and timeouts are computed and enforced in code. This judgment never authorizes tool execution or an unlimited loop.

title: Urgency and operational risk
when_to_use: Describe urgency and possible harm along separate, concrete dimensions.
notes: Do not infer real deadlines or compute elapsed time in the model. Use code-derived fields for timing. Synthetic examples are not safety certification.

title: Output verification and guardrails
when_to_use: Check a generated answer on independent dimensions before code applies policy.
notes: Code should perform exact format/schema checks and secret scanning too. A semantic judgment is one signal, not a complete security boundary. Example secrets below are deliberately fake.

title: RAG chunk relevance
when_to_use: Score each candidate chunk against the same query with a shared rubric.
notes: Retrieve candidates in code, score them, then sort by comparable scores. Reranking cannot recover missing evidence. The unrelated field is an intentional lesson distractor.

title: Groundedness checking
when_to_use: Check whether a single factual claim is supported by retrieved evidence.
notes: Split multi-claim answers in code. Check citation existence and literal quote presence in code before semantic support. Missing evidence counts as unsupported here.
